summary: ⚠️ THE STAGED BYTES MOVED UNDER ME MID-REVIEW: the packet was built for 04a22ee4 and the index now hashes to 8ced8150, with the row renumbered M0.65 -> M0.75 and four of the production round's findings already fixed. I reviewed the CURRENT bytes and re-derived the 202/201 count and the unattested '206-213' quotation independently before finding them already closed; I am not re-filing those, nor R-M4.45-1's truncated quotation, which the new M4.45 row now carries in full and correctly calls the worse half. No test bytes change, so there is no mutation to survive; this is a measurement-integrity review against `.harness/review/` and the tree. WHAT M4.45 GETS RIGHT, verified rather than assumed: the quotation is now verbatim including 'round-2 review measured exactly that' (FakeSequencerTest.java:206-210); the direction matches the landed record at backlog-done.md:110 ('8 of 8 fresh JVMs failing where the reviewer had measured 1 in 6 passing'), so surviving 1 in 6 is failing ~5 in 6; no assertion is affected -- the three `containsExactly` at :226-235 read the delta and deleting the comment entirely changes no outcome; the fixture is six keys and 6! = 720, which makes '1 in 720' the ESCAPE (pass) rate only under the correct reading; M4.8a (backlog-notes.md:321) states it the right way round in its own words; 17e54d6 records the failure twice (its four-false-claims paragraph and recorded minor 6); and `grep 'most times'` over *.java/*.md/*.txt outside .git and .harness returns exactly one surviving copy, FakeSequencerTest.java:209. WHAT M0.75 GETS RIGHT: 'load average 123' is TR-M4.17-3 (e8a3151c..., test-reviewer, 05:38), '186' is the M4.17 production summary (05:40), 'cannot flake on a loaded machine' is verbatim in 6e0d2ee2...reviewer.json, and /proc/loadavg still reads 8.08/99.67/162.98 -- a 15-minute average of 163 decaying from ~200, consistent with a very recent kill. TWO CLAUSES DO NOT HOLD, one carried over untouched and one introduced by this round's fixes; both are about which timing evidence a future session must re-make.

findings.summary: '`Thread.sleep` overruns rather than undershoots, so an honest rate measured under load is a FLOOR and the analysis is conservative' is not supported, and the record contradicts it in the direction that matters. (1) THE PREMISE APPLIES TO BOTH SIDES OF THE QUOTIENT. The quantity is `store.counts().puts()` differenced across `Thread.sleep(1000)` -- LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:415-419, whose own comment says 'THE SLEEP IS THE MEASUREMENT WINDOW, not synchronisation'. Overrun-not-undershoot lowers the count through the renewer's 150ms sleeps and RAISES it through the 1000ms window sleep. The premise fixes neither the sign nor the size of the quotient. (2) ON THE ROW'S OWN DATA THE LOADED RUNS ARE THE HIGH ONES. TR-M4.17-3 (.harness/review/e8a3151c...test-reviewer.json, 05:38) records 'Clean honest values: 6 (three idle runs), 6 (two runs under 32 spinners on 20 cores), 7 (two runs at load average 123)'. The load-measured value is the MAXIMUM observed there, not a floor. (3) SO A LANDED MARGIN IS ANTI-CONSERVATIVE, not merely mis-labelled, which is the question this row exists to answer. The committed slack figure is the load-measured 7: LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:389-390 reads 'Honest is 6-7 even at load / average 124, so a floor of 4 keeps ~1.75x slack', and the M4.17 production verdict says 'the honest run measured 7 three times at load average 186, so the floor keeps 1.75x slack'. 7/4 = 1.75; the idle sample gives 6/4 = 1.5. The tree carries the higher number. (4) THE CLASS THE ARGUMENT CANNOT COVER IS THE ONE THE ROW DOES NOT LIST. Everything named -- 'the renew-rate floor, honest 6-7/s values, and judgements that a bound cannot flake on a loaded machine' -- is honest-side. Mutant SURVIVAL counts run the other way: a stretched window can only ADD a tick, and adding one is exactly how a 2x mutant at 1000/300 = 3.33 reaches 4 and clears an inclusive floor of 4. M4.41 (backlog-notes.md:309) is built on that -- 'BIMODAL AT 3/4 ... fires ~40% of the time' -- from the 4,3,4,4,3 series in TR-M4.17-3 at 05:38, while the round before measured the SAME mutant 'green 5/5 on an idle machine with instrumented values fastRate=3 slowRate=0 every run' (TR-M4.17-6, 3893ebde..., 05:22, quoted in 56a8185d...test-reviewer.json). I am NOT claiming those 4s are artifacts: with a 300ms period in a 1000ms window, phase alone gives P(count = 4) ~ 1/3, so both series reconcile without any leak. That is the point -- it is open, and this clause tells the next session it need not be opened. (5) THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE PLUS TWO LOCATIONS. Say the sign is unknown because the window is a sleep too, and that the loaded runs measured HIGHER than the idle ones; and name where leak-window figures are COMMITTED, which the row still does not: LocalSequencerRenewTest.java:389-390 and baselines/review.txt:18 ('honest never below 6 including at load average 123'). Both evade the obvious grep -- the test comment wraps 'load' / 'average' across two comment lines, so `grep 'load average'` over that file returns NOTHING, and it says 124 where every verdict says 123. That is the escaping-a-grep failure the sibling M4.45 row in this same diff exists to record.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks up M4.41 -- an open row prescribing a coupled three-part test change (window to 2000ms, floor to 9, and moving `slowRate`'s `isLessThan(3L)`, which the row says goes red on a correct tree at 2000ms) -- reads M0.75 saying the direction is safe and the analysis conservative, and does not re-measure the 3/4 bimodality on a quiet machine. It widens a detector that may already have been adequate, and touches a second assertion to do it. In the other direction, a later session reads 'measured under load is a FLOOR', treats the committed '~1.75x slack' as a lower bound when the idle sample gives 1.5x, and tightens the floor or shortens the window on margin that is not there -- reinstating the flake this class already survived once.

findings.summary: THIS SENTENCE IS NEW IN THIS ROUND, IT IS FALSE, AND IT SHRINKS THE BLAST RADIUS AT EXACTLY THE POINT A LANDED PRESCRIPTION SITS. A reviewer verdict does record measuring at ~206: .harness/review/68c714405ad5156656e637e4fca90e16677c62935ba51cb5ea355d3ba1668557.reviewer.json, finding M4.43-R1d, mtime 05:59, reads 'I measured the same configuration in my own tree (2000ms window, `sleepFor(leases.renewInterval().multipliedBy(2))`, `--rerun-tasks`, values read from TEST-binjava.sequencer.LocalSequencerRenewTest.xml, load average ~206) and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7.' That is a reviewer, reporting its own timing measurement, naming the load it made it under, inside the window. The finding this sentence was written to fix said so: R-M0.65-4 (04a22ee4...reviewer.json) lists among what it COULD verify '"load average ~206) and got fast=6, fast=7, fast=7"', and says only that the quoted string '206-213' does not occur and that '~206' is the closest recorded figure. Dropping '206-213' was right; reattributing '~206' to this session's `uptime` overshoots into a claim the artifact contradicts. IT IS NOT COSMETIC. Those three runs are one of the two samples behind M4.41's '2x mutant `fastRate=7 slowRate=1` (3 of 3) in one tree and `fastRate=6,7,7` in another' and hence behind 'SO THE MUTANT IS 6 OR 7, BIMODAL AT 2000ms TOO ... A floor of 9 clears both modes' -- the remedy M4.41 prescribes. As written, this row tells a session that only two reviewer measurements were taken under the leak and that the 206 figure came from `uptime`, so the sample underlying the remedy is never questioned. Fix: 'load averages 123, 186 and ~206 all appear in recorded verdicts; the quoted range 206-213 does not, and is this session's own `uptime` reading rather than a reviewer's.'
findings.failure_scenario: The fix session for M4.41 enumerates which recorded measurements fall inside the leak window using this row as the index, finds 123 and 186 named and 206 explicitly excluded as 'this session's uptime', and re-makes only the 1000ms series. The 2000ms 6/7 bimodality -- measured at ~206 and the whole reason 'a floor of 9 clears both modes' rather than a floor of 8 or 7 -- is carried forward unexamined into the committed remedy. Second-order, and worse for this file's purpose: the row whose subject is 'reviewers believed a figure was ambient' now itself states, as fact about the archive, something the archive refutes, and a reader who checks one citation and finds it wrong discounts the two that are right.
